newsitem.title: CANADA: Wages divide Falconbridge, Dominican union.
newsitem.headline: Wages divide Falconbridge, Dominican union.

text.p: Wages are the main issue standing in the way of a new labor contract between Falconbridge and 1,000 unionized workers in the Dominican Republic, a Falconbridge spokesman said on Monday.

"We have offered to pay the union around cost-of-living, and they are requesting 25 percent in the first year, which is completely out of touch," said Bertrand de Windt, manager of human resources for Falconbridge Dominicana.
In a phone interview from Dominican Republic, de Windt said management and union officials would enter into a conciliation process starting on Wednesday.
"We have high hopes that we'll reach an agreement during conciliation," he said.
Inflation in that country is expected to be between two and five percent next year, and Falconbridge will use that figure as a basis for cost-of-living, de Windt said.
The workers are a long way from a strike, he added. Dominican labor law requires conciliation followed by arbitration before a union can request permission to strike.
The workers have been without a contract since the end of November.
In 1995, the Dominican facility produced 30,900 tonnes of nickel in ferronickel.
